claims.text: U.S. President Donald Trump signed into law the Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act, 2026.
The Act permits the U.S. to impose a 100% tariff on imports from countries that continue to import crude oil or natural gas from Russia 30 days after its enactment.
The Act originally aimed to cut off funding for Russia's war in Ukraine by sanctioning top Russian leadership and major energy customers.
The text of the Act was amended to extend sanctions on Iran for another five years until 2031.
Russia accounted for more than 51% of India's crude oil imports in July 2026.
India faces an existing 10% tariff under Section 301 of the Trade Act of 1974 and a 50% tariff under Section 232 of the Trade Expansion Act of 1962.

Union Minister of State for External Affairs Kirti Vardhan Singh stated that India considers the U.S. tariffs very unfair and will buy energy from commercially viable and economical sources independently.
The White House confirmed President Trump signed H.R. 5334, the Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act of 2026, into law on Friday, September 18, 2026.
The legislation cleared the U.S. Senate with an 86-11 vote in August and passed the House of Representatives 262-159.
Republican Senator Lindsey Graham, who spearheaded the bill, died in July 2026.

India's Ministry of External Affairs stated that New Delhi is committed to ensuring energy security through diversified sourcing and market dynamics, and will take all necessary steps to protect its economic interests.
The Trump administration imposed a 25% punitive tariff on India in August 2025 over Russian oil imports, which Trump removed in February 2026 following an interim trade deal.
India's Russian oil imports reached an 11-month high in April 2026 following the U.S. and Israel war on Iran, after dropping to a 38-month low in December 2025.
The Akhil Bharatiya Vidyarthi Parishad (ABVP) won three central panel posts in the Delhi University Students' Union (DUSU) elections.
Independent candidate Deepanshu Shokeen won the DUSU vice-presidential post with 30,615 votes, defeating ABVP's Ishu Maurya who received 16,901 votes.
ABVP's Yash Dabas was elected DUSU president with 24,576 votes, defeating NSUI's Vijay Shankar Meena who received 22,523 votes.
ABVP's Riya Chhawdi won the DUSU secretary post with 21,650 votes against NSUI's Namrata Chaudhary who received 14,869 votes.
ABVP's Lakshay Raj Singh won the joint secretary post by a margin of 837 votes against Vishesh Yadav of Samajwadi Chhatra Sabha.
Voter turnout for the DUSU elections was 40.46%, compared to 39.5% in the previous year.
The National Students' Union of India (NSUI) drew a blank in the Delhi University Students' Union central panel elections.
Union Home Minister Amit Shah congratulated ABVP, stating the victory reflects youth trust in the council's Nation First ideology.
Deepanshu Shokeen chose to run as an independent candidate after learning on September 11 that he was denied a ticket by NSUI.
Deepanshu Shokeen hails from Peeragarhi village in west Delhi, where his father works as a bus conductor and his mother as an Anganwadi teacher.
More than 2,000 police and paramilitary personnel were deployed across Delhi University during the vote counting process.
CJP co-convenor Saurav Das stated on X that a majority of students opposed the current regime but their votes were fractured.
Yash Dabas is an international-level tennis player who represented Delhi University at the Khelo India University Games and All-India University Games.
Yash Dabas completed his undergraduate degree at Sri Guru Tegh Bahadur Khalsa College and is pursuing an MA in Buddhist Studies at Delhi University.
DUSU President-elect Yash Dabas announced that his first priority would be conducting a safety audit of all college hostels and paying guest accommodations.
